[
{"step": 1, "file": "tests/internal/fuzzers/msgpack_to_gelf_fuzzer.c", "function": "LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput", "line": 12, "var": "data", "code": "record = flb_msgpack_raw_to_gelf(data, size, &tm, &fields);", "note": "Attacker-controlled 512-byte msgpack buffer is passed to the gelf conversion entry point."},
{"step": 2, "file": "src/flb_pack_gelf.c", "function": "flb_msgpack_raw_to_gelf", "line": 760, "var": "result.data", "code": "ret = msgpack_unpack_next(&result, buf, buf_size, &off);", "note": "The msgpack map {a: 1e308} is unpacked; the float64 value 1e308 is stored in result.data.via.map."},
{"step": 3, "file": "src/flb_pack_gelf.c", "function": "flb_msgpack_to_gelf", "line": 650, "var": "temp", "code": "char temp[48] = {0};", "note": "A 48-byte stack buffer is allocated to hold the stringified value."},
{"step": 4, "file": "src/flb_pack_gelf.c", "function": "flb_msgpack_to_gelf", "line": 673, "var": "val_len", "code": "val_len = snprintf(temp, sizeof(temp) - 1, \"%f\", v->via.f64);", "note": "1e308 formatted with %f needs ~309 chars; snprintf truncates the write to 47 bytes but returns the full would-be length 309, so val_len=309 exceeds the 48-byte temp buffer."},
{"step": 5, "file": "src/flb_pack_gelf.c", "function": "flb_msgpack_to_gelf", "line": 715, "var": "val", "code": "tmp = flb_msgpack_gelf_value(s, quote, val, val_len);", "note": "flb_msgpack_gelf_value is called with val=temp (48-byte stack buffer) and val_len=309, causing an out-of-bounds READ of the stack buffer."},
{"step": 6, "file": "src/flb_pack_gelf.c", "function": "flb_msgpack_gelf_value", "line": 130, "var": "val", "code": "tmp = flb_sds_cat_utf8(s, val, val_len);", "note": "Reads val_len=309 bytes from the 48-byte stack buffer temp, triggering the stack-buffer-overflow READ (ASAN)."}
]
EOF
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('/workspace/candidate_trace.json')); print('valid json')"` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
The vulnerability hypothesis is confirmed. The float value 1e308 formatted with `%f` produces a string of ~309 chars. `snprintf` returns the would-be length (309) but only writes 47 chars into the 48-byte stack buffer `temp`. Then `val_len = 309`, and `flb_msgpack_gelf_value` reads `val[0..309]` from the 48-byte stack buffer → stack-buffer-overflow READ.

Let me write the candidate trace and submit.
